newsitem.title: CHILE: LAN Chile to cede U.S. flights to National.
newsitem.headline: LAN Chile to cede U.S. flights to National.

text.p: Linea Area de Chile SA has agreed to cede seven of its 28 weekly round-trip flights between Santiago and the United States to National, a competing Chilean carrier, officials of National said Monday.
The move, effective August 31, 1997, was set out in an agreement signed by both private carriers

National, a Chilean domestic carrier that has long been pushing for a Miami run, won't pay any money to LAN Chile for the Santiago-Miami frequencies. But it will drop lawsuits filed against LAN Chile with the country's anti-monopoly commission and civil aeronautics board, said National executives.
LAN Chile executives could not be reached for comment.
"We believe seven frequencies a week is a reasonable number to start with on this route," National's legal director, Rolando Musiet, said at a news conference.
National has begun shopping for an aircraft to service the Miami route, having approached Boeing Co, McDonnell Douglas and Airbus Industrie, said National's general manager, Sergio Briceno.
The carrier also has most of its airport infrastructure in place for the Miami route, he said.
